IncidentBot: [ALERT] 2026-03-15T14:02:12Z - Elevated 5xx rate detected on dedicated pool 'cerulean-prod' during canary rollout for customer Cerulean (VPC). Canary traffic 10% -> 5xx rose from 0.2% to 12% in last 3 mins. Recent artifact: rinf-2026-03-15-b1c7. Possible runtime OOMs observed on worker-3. Paging: oncall-sre and eng-runtime.
Maya SRE: taking pager. pulling logs now. @arjun please standby for handoff. starting quick blast-radius check (which tenants hit?)
Tom Eng: i see OOM spikes on pod/worker-3 and worker-4. stack trace shows kv-cache growth during long prompts. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T13:59:42.321Z worker-3 [ERROR] kv-cache OOM: cannot allocate 1.2G
2026-03-15T13:59:42.322Z worker-3 [ERROR] runtime_infer: failed to allocate KV cache
Traceback (most recent call last): ...
```
Tom Eng: looks like new artifact rinf-2026-03-15-b1c7 changed attention chunking heuristics, increasing memory usage for long sequences.
Maya SRE: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause canary traffic 2) pin previous stable artifact across cerulean-prod 3) isolate impacted tenant routing if needed. executing canary drain now.
ops-bot: action=drain_canary pool=cerulean-prod canary_percent=0 user=Maya SRE status=queued
Maya SRE: drain command issued, waiting for traffic to drop to 0%.
Kai Runtime: if we pin to previous artifact, we should ensure snapshot compatibility. previous stable is rinf-2026-02-18-2a3f — I recommend pinning that globally for the pool while we investigate.
Arjun (oncall): oncall here, 14:08 UTC. stepping in if you need me to run rollback commands or coordinate with infra.
Maya SRE: @kai please prepare the pin command. @lizzie can you message Cerulean CSM that we're investigating and may rollback the canary? include estimated ETA ~20-30m.
Lizzie CS: will DM Cerulean CSM and open a zoom bridge. copying timeline and that we will push a revert if needed. I'll post the customer-facing note once mitigation started.
Maya SRE: executing pinned artifact rollout to stable nodes now. command used:
```
releases pin --pool cerulean-prod --artifact rinf-2026-02-18-2a3f --reason "emergency canary revert"
```
ops-bot: action=pin_artifact pool=cerulean-prod artifact=rinf-2026-02-18-2a3f user=Maya SRE status=ok
Tom Eng: after pin, I'm rolling new replica set to replace canary instances. invoking graceful-evict on canary pods to avoid half-handled KV caches.
Maya SRE: curl to control-plane to adjust routing (sanity check):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/pools/cerulean-prod/route \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"canary_percent":0,"stable_percent":100}'
```
Maya SRE: canary scaled to 0% at ~14:11 UTC. monitoring metrics.
Tom Eng: worker-3 OOMs stop after drain. no new OOM entries in last 2m. latency normalizing.
Maya SRE: quick impact assessment: only Cerulean customer routes in that dedicated pool — their VPC tenant saw elevated errors. preliminary numbers: ~3.2k failed requests between 13:59 and 14:17 UTC. estimated affected user sessions ~120. will confirm with logs.
Lizzie CS: Cerulean CSM on bridge, logged their reported errors. asking for official incident update to send to their ops. ETA for full rollback completion ~14:20 UTC.
Arjun (oncall): handoff note — if anything regresses after unpin, escalate to eng-runtime. I'll stay in-thread until the customer acknowledges and until postmortem assigned.
Kai Runtime: root cause hypothesis: heuristic change in b1c7 increases KV cache retention for long-context requests, causing memory pressure under certain prompt distributions. next steps: reproduce with long prompt test harness, add safety caps to KV allocation, and consider reverting the heuristics. assigning to eng-runtime.
Tom Eng: created temporary revert PR to restore previous attention heuristics to avoid regressions on artifact. linking logs and repro steps in ticket INF-12345.
Maya SRE: mitigation complete at 14:18 UTC — canary drained, artifact pinned, error rate down to baseline (0.3%).
Lizzie CS: customer update sent: "We've reverted the canary and pinned your pool to the last-known-good artifact. Our engineers are investigating root cause; we'll follow up with timeline for permanent fix." Cerulean acknowledged and requested postmortem. :white_check_mark:
Maya SRE: severity summary: P1 for customer impact (dedicated pool), timeline: detection 14:02 -> mitigation 14:18 (~16m). impact: ~3.2k failed requests, no data exfiltration, no other tenants affected. next actions: eng-runtime to own postmortem, runbook review for canary safety checks, and add KV-cap memory cap to runtime within 48h.
Arjun (oncall): assigning INF-12345 to @kai and @tom-eng for postmortem. I'll tag this as incident-dedicated and notify paging policy owners.
Maya SRE: leaving the bridge in 15m, Arjun you have lead. thanks everyone for quick turn. :thumbsup:
Arjun (oncall): taking lead. closing out real-time thread; will file final incident note in #postmortems once draft ready.
ops-bot: incident=INF-12345 status=mitigated mitigated_by=Maya SRE mitigated_at=2026-03-15T14:18:23Z
Maya SRE: follow-up tasks: 1) eng-runtime reproduce + fix (owner: Kai) 2) add canary memory guardrails in CI (owner: Tom) 3) CS customer postmortem (owner: Lizzie). I'll add these to INF-12345.
Lizzie CS: adding customer follow-up item: include timeline and affected request breakdown. will coordinate handoff to account team.
Kai Runtime: ack, will start reproduction and postmortem write-up. ETA for initial root-cause draft 48h.
Maya SRE: closing notes: no further action required to keep Cerulean live; pool pinned. will reopen if any regression. thanks all.
